title: The Missing Croak Chorus
markdown:
Gather ‘round, because this story is about a swamp so sunny, it’s called Sunnybrook. And guess what? It’s about to have a very big problem! This problem is so big, it makes a tadpole look like a speck of dust!

Now, in Sunnybrook Swamp, where the lily pads giggled like sleepy green tummies and the dragonflies zipped by like tiny, whizzing, jeweled airplanes, there was a very important event that everyone looked forward to. Every single year, the swamp held the most fabulous, the most fun, the most swampy singing contest known to amphibian and insect kind: The Song of the Swamps! The heart of this contest was the Great Swamp Songbook. It was sparkly, splashy, and wonderfully watery – the very soul of the Song of the Swamps! Imagine a book made of reeds and whispers, its pages filled with the songs that made all the swamp creatures want to sing along!

Who looked after this special book? It was Fern the Frog! Fern wasn't just any frog. He was the swamp's librarian. He had the shiniest, greenest skin and the biggest, roundest glasses you ever did see. They sat right on his nose like two little water bubbles! He loved that songbook more than a fly loves a warm, lazy afternoon. He polished its pages with the freshest morning dew drops until they gleamed, and he tucked it in at night with a gentle, contented croak-croak-croak. He treated it like a VIP – a Very Important Page-holder!

This year, the Song of the Swamps was extra special. It was the big centennial celebration! Everyone knew that the winning song, the song that would become legendary, would be sung from the very last page of the book – the magnificent, the mysterious, the utterly "croakiest" of them all: the "Croakiest Croak Chorus." Oh, it was a masterpiece, a symphony of the swamp! It was full of deep, rumbling burps that made the mudbanks vibrate, and high, reedy eeks that tickled your ears. It made your toes wiggle and your nose twitch, it was THAT good! The whole swamp hummed with excitement just thinking about it.

But then… Big trouble! A huge disaster! One bright, cheerful morning, Fern was happily fluttering through the pages of the songbook, humming a little tune he’d made up about a particularly plump dragonfly. He was ready to practice the star of the show, the Croakiest Croak Chorus. He reached the very back, and he stopped. His little froggy jaw dropped so far, you could have dropped a pebble into it! His glasses wobbled unsteadily, almost falling into the pond. His heart went thump-thump-thumpety-thump – faster than a dragonfly’s wings!

"My page!" he gasped, his voice a strangled squeak. "My… my CROAKIEST PAGE! It's GONE! Vanished! POOF!"

It was true! The most beautiful, the most important, the most wonderfully, gloriously croaky page of the entire songbook had vanished like a puff of swamp mist on a windy day. The whole swamp seemed to hold its breath. A hush fell over the giggling lily pads, and they drooped just a little. The dragonflies flew a little slower, their usual zipping replaced by a mournful zigzag. A big, dark cloud seemed to hover right over Fern’s favorite mossy log.

Now, a little way up, in a tall, twisty willow tree whose branches tickled the clouds, lived Mina the Magpie. Mina loved shiny things. Oh, she loved them so much, her eyes would sparkle brighter than any gem! A dewdrop clinging to a spiderweb? Sparkly perfection! A fallen beetle's iridescent wing? Gleaming treasure! A lost button that tumbled from a picnicker’s coat? Absolute bliss! Her nest wasn't just twigs and fluff; it was a dazzling treasure trove, a glittering museum of all things bright and beautiful that caught her eye.

And guess what Mina found that very same morning, nestled amongst her collection of sparkly river pebbles and bits of crumpled foil? A very large, very colourful, and very shiny piece of paper. It shimmered and shimmered in the dappled sunlight filtering through the leaves, and it had some very peculiar, wiggly squiggles and dotty patterns on it that looked like a secret code. "Ooh!" chirped Mina, her black eyes gleaming with delight. "This is positively dazzling! The most magnificent shimmer I've seen all week!" She tucked it carefully into her nest, right next to a particularly glittery piece of broken blue glass that she called her "sky shard."

Meanwhile, Fern was hopping from one lily pad to another, looking utterly miserable. He sighed so deeply, he blew a small ripple across the water. "No Croakiest Croak Chorus," he mumbled, his voice a little shaky, like a wobbly jelly. "No contest. What will we sing? What will Sunnybrook Swamp sing without its heart-song?" He felt a tiny tear well up behind his glasses.

Mina watched from her high perch in the willow tree. She saw Fern looking so sad, his shoulders slumped. She heard the other swamp creatures sighing and murmuring amongst themselves. She looked down at her prize, that shiny, intriguing paper that felt so special. It had that unique oomph that all her best treasures had, that undeniable pull. But as she looked at it, and then back at Fern’s forlorn face, something felt a little bit wrong. It looked, she admitted to herself with a tiny frown, remarkably like the kind of important paper a librarian frog would cherish.

The day of the Song of the Swamps contest dawned, and the air was thick with a strange mixture of anticipation and gloom. The usual cheerful buzz of excitement was muted, replaced by worried whispers. Mina could hear the sad chirps and croaks from below, a symphony of sadness. She looked at her nest, at the dazzling paper. And then she looked at Fern, who was trying his very best to smile for the other contestants, but his glasses were still a little foggy with worry, and his usual bouncy hop was more of a sad shuffle.

Suddenly, Mina’s heart did a funny little flip. It wasn't the usual excited flip she felt when she spotted something new and shiny. It was a different kind of flip. A warmer, wobblier, almost ticklish flip. She imagined Fern’s face if he saw the page again, the pure joy that would spread across it. She imagined the happy ribbiting and cheerful buzzing that would echo through the swamp if the contest could go on, with its very best song! It would be a much more magnificent sound than any sparkle she could collect.

"OH! OH! This is not good," Mina whispered to herself, a tiny puff of dust escaping her beak as she ruffled her feathers. "Shiny is nice, very, very nice. But… but happy is even shinier! And seeing Fern so sad is… well, it’s the opposite of shiny!" She realized with a jolt that her shiny treasure was making others feel dim.

She knew, with a certainty that surprised her, what she had to do. It wasn't an easy decision. It meant giving up the most beautiful, most mysterious, most sparkly thing she had found all year. It meant letting go of a treasure that glittered in her nest. But friendships, Mina suddenly understood with a clear heart, were even more precious than any treasure she could hoard. They were like sunshine, making everything brighter.

With a determined flutter and a confident swoop, Mina the Magpie grabbed the special page. She soared through the air, a black-and-white streak against the blue sky, past the giggling lily pads that seemed to gasp in surprise, and landed with a soft thud right in front of Fern, who was looking utterly bewildered at the sight of her.

"Fern!" Mina chirped, her voice a little nervous, a little shaky, but firm. "I… I found this. In my nest. I think… I think it’s yours. I picked it up because it was so shiny, and I just… well, I forgot how important it was to you and the swamp. I'm so, so sorry. I hope you can forgive me!" She held out the page, its edges slightly rumpled from its adventure in the nest.

Fern blinked. He blinked again. His glasses fogged up completely with emotion, then cleared. And then, his froggy face broke into the biggest, widest, most joyous smile Sunnybrook Swamp had ever, ever seen! It was a smile that stretched from his chin to the tips of his long, wobbly ears!

"MY PAGE!" he croaked, his voice bursting with pure, complete delight, like a popped bubble of happiness. "You found it! Oh, Mina! Thank you, thank you, THANK YOU!" He carefully took the page, his little froggy fingers trembling with relief, and smoothed it out. The familiar, wonderful squiggles and dots seemed to wink at him, as if to say, "We're back!"

The whole swamp erupted in cheers! A tidal wave of ribbits and chirps and happy buzzes filled the air, a magnificent mix of sounds of joy! The lily pads bounced with glee, and the dragonflies performed celebratory loop-de-loops, their wings catching the sunlight like a thousand tiny diamonds. Fern, with the Croakiest Croak Chorus page safely back in its rightful place, beamed at Mina, his eyes shining brighter than his glasses.

"You know, Mina," Fern said, his voice warm and full of gratitude. "You're not just a magpie who loves shiny things. You're a friend who knows what's truly important. And that is the most valuable treasure of all."

Mina puffed out her chest, not with pride, but with a warm, bubbly happiness that felt even better than finding the shiniest pebble. She hadn't won the contest, not by a long shot. But she had helped save it. And that, she decided with a contented sigh, was far, far better than any sparkly trinket she could ever collect.

And so, the Song of the Swamps contest went ahead, with Fern and all the creatures singing the Croakiest Croak Chorus with all their might, their voices soaring through the sunny air. And the sweetest, most wonderful sound of all that day? It was the sound of friendship, shining brighter than any treasure, in the happy, musical heart of Sunnybrook Swamp.
characters: Mina the magpie, Fern the frog
